intro: The Bengals buried the Steelers to take sole control of the AFC North, and the Lions lost edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a reported season-ending knee injury in Munich. Baltimore starts Jacoby Brissett on Monday night against the winless Chargers. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Bengals rout Steelers 38-18 and take the AFC North alone
top.dek: Cincinnati won its fifth straight and moved to 7-2, one game clear of Pittsburgh. Joe Burrow went 35 of 44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns before Joe Flacco finished the game.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lions lose Aidan Hutchinson to a reported season-ending knee injury
top.dek: Hutchinson hurt his right knee landing from a sack celebration in Munich and left on crutches. The AP, citing an anonymous source, reported the injury as season-ending, but the Lions have not confirmed a diagnosis.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Ja'Marr Chase piles up 231 yards on 11 catches
top.dek: Chase gained 146 of those yards in the first half, and one 53-yard catch set up a Bengals score. Pittsburgh never found an answer for him or for Burrow.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 389: Brock Purdy sets a career high in the 49ers' 46-40 win in Dallas
top.dek: Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes without an interception and averaged almost 14 yards per attempt. Christian McCaffrey scored three times as San Francisco moved to 8-1.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Brissett starts for Baltimore against the winless Chargers tonight
top.dek: The Chargers visit the Ravens on Monday Night Football at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Lamar Jackson is out six to ten weeks with a thumb injury, so veteran Jacoby Brissett takes over for a Baltimore team on a four-game losing streak.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hit 8-1 with a road rout of the Jets

stories.text: Bills beat the Jets 31-12 for their best start since 1991
stories.summary: Buffalo trailed 10-9 early in the third quarter at MetLife Stadium, then scored three touchdowns in the second half to pull away. The Bills are 8-1 and still unbeaten on the road this season at 5-0. Josh Allen ran for two scores and threw a 45-yard touchdown to DJ Moore, and Buffalo has beaten the Jets six straight times.

stories.text: Two corners leave the Jets game, and a linebacker is questionable
stories.summary: Cornerback Dee Alford went out in the second half after a second hit to the head and was ruled out with a concussion. Cornerback Christian Benford left in the fourth quarter with a groin issue. Linebacker Dorian Williams was listed questionable to return with a calf injury. Official designations for the Dolphins game come later this week.

stories.text: James Cook runs for 157 yards and a 74-yard score
stories.summary: Cook carried 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown against the Jets. His 74-yard run came 10 seconds after New York fumbled a lateral, and it was the longest Buffalo run this season. He is the first player since LaDainian Tomlinson in 2006 to post 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in eight straight games.

stories.text: 202: yards on three second-half scoring drives of seven plays total
stories.summary: Buffalo scored on drives of four plays, two plays and one play after halftime, covering 62, 66 and 74 yards. The three drives took 2:49 of game time. The Bills converted only 2 of 10 third downs and still averaged 7.2 yards a play.

stories.text: Dolphins visit Buffalo on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami comes to Highmark Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Bills have outscored their last two opponents 54-18 and have not allowed an offensive touchdown in eight quarters. Watch whether Buffalo keeps that run going against a Dolphins offense that started Kyle McCord at quarterback Sunday.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins fall 24-22 as McCord makes first start

stories.text: Dolphins lose 24-22 to Colts and drop to 1-8
stories.summary: Miami never led in Kyle McCord's first career start. A strip-sack gave Indianapolis a 21-7 lead in the third quarter, and a late McCord touchdown run cut it to two. The Dolphins could not convert after that, and the Colts snapped a five-game losing streak.

stories.text: Zach Sieler is out for the season with a biceps injury
stories.summary: The Dolphins lost defensive tackle Zach Sieler for the year. Zeek Biggers (knee) and Jordan Phillips (arm) also got hurt Sunday, which thins the interior further. Center Aaron Brewer missed the game with a concussion, and Andrew Meyer started in his place and played through a stinger.

stories.text: Chop Robinson has four sacks in his last four games
stories.summary: Robinson picked up his fifth sack of the season against Indianapolis, plus five tackles and two quarterback hits. His pass rush win rate of about 36 percent leads the league. Miami's defense also held Daniel Jones to 108 passing yards and two interceptions.

stories.text: 7: points Zane Gonzalez's three misses cost Miami
stories.summary: Gonzalez missed a 47-yard field goal, a 51-yarder and an extra point in a two-point loss. He went 1 of 3 on field goals and has missed kicks in three straight games. He is Miami's second kicker this season, after Riley Patterson was waived following Week 5.

stories.text: Miami visits Buffalo on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Dolphins play at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the line of scrimmage, where Miami is down to thin tackle depth against a Bills offense that rushed well Sunday. The Dolphins then host the Jets in Week 12.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots routed 35-10 in Munich, Maye hurt

stories.text: Patriots lose Drake Maye and the game in Munich, 35-10
stories.summary: Maye left in the first quarter with an ankle injury after a sack by Aidan Hutchinson, and Tommy DeVito finished the game. Detroit gained 494 yards. New England has now allowed 35 or more points in back-to-back games for the first time since 1994, and it sits at 5-5.

stories.text: Maye needs more tests, and A.J. Brown has a hamstring issue
stories.summary: Mike Vrabel said Maye could not function and that the team will run more tests back in New England. Receiver A.J. Brown left in the second half with a hamstring problem, and the staff will check its severity later this week. Rhamondre Stevenson had only six carries for 4 yards in the game.

stories.text: Will Campbell has a rough day at left tackle
stories.summary: Left tackle Will Campbell allowed six pressures and two sacks against Detroit. One of the sacks came from Hutchinson and ended with Maye leaving the field. Campbell had also left the Week 9 loss to Green Bay with a knee injury.

stories.text: 494: yards Detroit gained, most vs. New England in regulation since Super Bowl LII
stories.summary: The Lions piled up 494 yards while the Patriots managed 151. Jared Goff threw for 303 yards and three touchdowns, and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and two scores. Detroit also won time of possession by about six minutes.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then at the Chargers on Nov. 29
stories.summary: New England is off next week. The Patriots return Sunday, Nov. 29 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC at the Chargers. Vrabel said the team must clean up turnovers, the run game, protection and third-down defense during the break, and the status of Maye is the question that matters.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets lose fifth straight, Geno Smith hurt

stories.text: Jets fall 31-12 to the Bills as Geno Smith leaves hurt
stories.summary: Smith took a hit before halftime and was checked for a head injury. He came back for a drive, then left in the third quarter with an ankle injury. Rookie Cade Klubnik took over and made his NFL debut. The Jets dropped to 2-8 with their fifth straight loss, and the offense produced only four Jason Sanders field goals.

stories.text: Smith (ankle), Cooper (ankle) and Parham (knee) all got hurt
stories.summary: Smith was ruled out after his ankle injury and finished 13 of 21 for 148 yards. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. hurt an ankle on the first offensive play, and left guard Dylan Parham hurt a knee early in the second quarter. Aaron Glenn will pick a starter for Sunday based on how Smith's ankle responds.

stories.text: Garrett Wilson catches 7 passes for 106 yards
stories.summary: Wilson had a 33-yard catch in the first half and a 29-yarder in the second, and both set up field goals. It was his second 100-yard game of the year. He also owned a fourth-quarter hook-and-lateral that Buffalo recovered before James Cook ran 74 yards for a touchdown. Wilson said he flubbed it.

stories.text: 9: straight quarters without a Jets offensive touchdown
stories.summary: New York's four scores against Buffalo were all Sanders field goals, so the drought has reached nine quarters. The Jets also went 0 for 2 in the red zone. Klubnik finished 11 of 20 for 137 yards with one interception and ran three times for 26 yards.

stories.text: Jets visit the winless Chargers Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: New York plays at Los Angeles on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox. The Chargers are 0-8, so this is a winnable game for a team on a five-game skid. The quarterback is the thing to watch, with Klubnik a possible first-time starter if Smith cannot go.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Brissett starts as Ravens try to end 4-game skid

stories.text: Ravens turn to Brissett with Jackson out 6 to 10 weeks
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson fractured and dislocated his right thumb on his first snap back from a high ankle sprain, then had surgery. Coach Jesse Minter says that kind of recovery usually takes six to ten weeks. Baltimore has lost four straight and sits one game out of the last AFC playoff spot, so veteran Jacoby Brissett starts tonight.

stories.text: Hawkins out, Randall questionable for Monday night
stories.summary: Safety Jaylinn Hawkins is out with a knee injury and will miss his fourth straight game. Rookie running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring) is questionable, and Minter said there is potential he gets activated for his first regular-season game. Receiver Rashod Bateman (calf) and guard Vega Ioane (knee and shoulder) were limited Thursday.

stories.text: Brissett takes a crash course in the Ravens offense
stories.summary: Jacoby Brissett landed in Baltimore after a trade, a week after Arizona made him its No. 3 quarterback. He threw for 215 yards a game in eight games with the Cardinals. He has stayed after practice to throw with receivers and work with coordinator Declan Doyle. Calais Campbell, his old Arizona teammate, says Brissett is ripping the ball.

stories.text: 13: most points Baltimore has scored in its four straight losses
stories.summary: The Ravens have not topped 13 points during the skid. The passing game managed 68 yards in Buffalo and 55 against Jacksonville with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano under center. Brissett has to lift that floor right away.

stories.text: Monday night at home against the winless Chargers
stories.summary: Baltimore hosts Los Angeles tonight on Monday Night Football (8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN per the league schedule). The Chargers are 0-8 and led by a coaching staff that faces its former defensive coordinator, Jesse Minter. The teams carry a combined 15 straight losses, a Monday night record per Sportradar. The Ravens visit Carolina in Week 11.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals bury Steelers, take sole lead in the North

stories.text: Bengals rout Steelers 38-18 and own the AFC North alone
stories.summary: Cincinnati won its fifth straight and moved into sole possession of first place at 7-2. Joe Burrow went 35 of 44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns before Joe Flacco finished the game. Burrow said the team is not satisfied with where it stands.

stories.text: Higgins limps off, Taylor says it is not serious
stories.summary: Tee Higgins hurt his knee and went to the locker room before halftime after five catches for 66 yards. Coach Zac Taylor said the team was managing his workload with a big lead, and he expects Higgins to play Monday at Washington. Guard Dalton Risner also left with a knee injury, and linebacker Oren Burks (groin) was ruled out.

stories.text: Chase posts 231 yards on 11 catches
stories.summary: Ja'Marr Chase had the most receiving yards of any player in the league this season, gaining 146 of them in the first half. One 53-yard catch came on a scoring drive. Pittsburgh could not find an answer for him or for Burrow.

stories.text: 5: straight games with 30 or more points, a team record
stories.summary: Cincinnati is the only team in the league with five straight 30-point games this season, and no Bengals team had done it before. Burrow leads the league with 27 touchdown passes. Chase Brown caught two touchdown passes in the win.

stories.text: Monday night at Washington in Week 11
stories.summary: Cincinnati visits the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23 (8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN per the league schedule). Watch Higgins's knee and the guard spot if Risner is out. The Bengals then host New Orleans and visit Cleveland on Dec. 6.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns erase 17-point hole, hit bye at 6-4

stories.text: Browns rally from 17 down to beat Houston 27-24
stories.summary: Cleveland trailed 17-0 and won on a fourth-quarter drive that Deshaun Watson sparked with a 30-yard throw to Harold Fannin Jr. Quinshon Judkins scored the winner. The Browns hold the third AFC wild-card spot going into their bye. It was their fourth double-digit comeback win of the year, a franchise record.

stories.text: Hickman in concussion protocol, Burton out before the bye
stories.summary: Safety Ronnie Hickman was in the concussion protocol and fullback Michael Burton was out with a calf injury for the Houston game. Receiver Denzel Boston, questionable with a toe injury, was trending in the right direction according to Todd Monken. The bye gives all three extra recovery time.

stories.text: Schwesinger tallies 13 tackles in the comeback
stories.summary: Carson Schwesinger had eight solo and five assisted tackles, both team highs. It was his sixth double-digit tackle game of the season and his third in a row. The Browns held Houston to one touchdown over the final two quarters.

stories.text: 55: straight games without allowing a 300-yard passer
stories.summary: Cleveland's streak is the longest active run in the league. C.J. Stroud threw for 190 yards in the first half and only 21 in the second. The Browns finished with nine passes defensed.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then Las Vegas at home
stories.summary: Cleveland is off this week. It returns Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox against the Raiders, per the league schedule, then hosts Cincinnati on Dec. 6 in a game that could decide first place in the North.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers stumble in Cincinnati, need a quick reset

stories.text: Steelers fall 38-18 in Cincinnati and lose the division lead
stories.summary: Pittsburgh entered 6-2 on a four-game winning streak and left 6-3, a game behind the Bengals. It was the Steelers' most lopsided loss of the season. Mike McCarthy said the performance fell short of the team's standard and blamed mechanical and operational lapses.

stories.text: Left guard McCormick carted off with an ankle injury
stories.summary: Mason McCormick hurt his right ankle late in the first half and left the field on a cart with an air cast. McCarthy gave no update and said the team would speak on it when the time is right. Spencer Anderson replaced him and is the likely starter if McCormick misses time.

stories.text: Metcalf and Freiermuth supply the late touchdowns
stories.summary: DK Metcalf caught a 32-yard pass in the fourth quarter, then a fourth-down touchdown from Aaron Rodgers, and Rodgers also threw him the two-point conversion. Pat Freiermuth added a 27-yard touchdown with 7:19 left. Rodgers finished 15 of 29 with two touchdowns and no interceptions.

stories.text: 38-18: a final score the NFL had never produced
stories.summary: The result was a Scorigami, the first game in league history to end 38-18. Cincinnati led by 21 at halftime and 31-3 later. Pittsburgh did not score a touchdown until the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Sunday at Philadelphia, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh visits the Eagles in Week 11 on Nov. 22 at Lincoln Financial Field. The league moved the game to a 1 p.m. kickoff for Salute to Service. The Steelers then host Denver on Nov. 27 on Prime Video.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans blow 17-0 lead in Cleveland

stories.text: Texans give away a 17-0 lead in Cleveland
stories.summary: Houston led 17-0 and lost 27-24 when Quinshon Judkins ran in from five yards with 53 seconds left. The Texans fell to 3-6 and put up six three-and-outs in the second half, including their last two possessions. C.J. Stroud said afterward the team did not adjust and that time is running out.

stories.text: Marks enters concussion protocol, Al-Shaair hurt
stories.summary: Running back Woody Marks went into the concussion protocol in the third quarter after a helmet-to-helmet hit. Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair also left, and Jake Hansen filled in. Edge rusher Danielle Hunter, guard Wyatt Teller and receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. all missed the game.

stories.text: Nico Collins draws 16 targets, catches nine
stories.summary: Collins caught 9 of 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown against Cleveland. He opened the scoring in the first quarter. He also cut short a route that led to Stroud's interception, a mistake that likely cost Houston at least a field goal before halftime.

stories.text: 21: Stroud's second-half passing yards
stories.summary: Stroud threw for 190 of his 211 yards in the first half and only 21 in the second. He went 5 of 19 after halftime. Houston ran for 88 net yards on the day and scored one touchdown over the final two quarters.

stories.text: Colts visit Houston Thursday night
stories.summary: Houston hosts Indianapolis on Thursday, Nov. 19 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Colts beat the Texans 19-17 in Week 3, and Houston has four days to fix a second-half offense that went quiet. Watch the status of Marks, Hunter and Harrison.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts end five-game skid, edge Miami

stories.text: Colts snap five-game losing streak, beat Miami 24-22
stories.summary: Indianapolis held off Miami at Lucas Oil Stadium for its third win of the year. A fumble return for a touchdown by Adetomiwa Adebawore and a 59-yard pick-six by Chris Johnson did much of the scoring. Miami kicker Zane Gonzalez missed a 51-yarder that could have tied it.

stories.text: No new Colts injuries reported after Miami
stories.summary: The game coverage reported no new Colts injuries beyond an early Jonathan Taylor fumble, which Indianapolis recovered. Taylor went on to carry 16 times for 83 yards. The first injury report for Thursday's short week will set the picture.

stories.text: Rookie Seth McGowan scores again
stories.summary: McGowan ran 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown, a career high in yards and his second straight week in the end zone. Taylor added 83 yards on 16 carries. The pair gave the Colts a ground game while the passing attack stalled.

stories.text: 108: Daniel Jones's passing yards in the win
stories.summary: Jones completed 11 of 22 passes for 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, and also lost a fumble. The Colts still won because the defense and special teams scored 14 points. Laquon Treadwell caught his first touchdown since 2021.

stories.text: Short week, at Houston Thursday night
stories.summary: Indianapolis visits Houston on Thursday, Nov. 19 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Colts beat the Texans 19-17 in Week 3. Houston just blew a 17-0 lead in Cleveland.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Lawrence throws for 352 in rout of Titans

stories.text: Jaguars roll Titans 40-23 for fifth straight series win
stories.summary: Jacksonville won its third in a row and sixth in seven games. The Jaguars now lead the AFC South by four games over Houston. The fifth straight win over Tennessee is a franchise record for the series.

stories.text: Hainsey and Striggow leave in Nashville
stories.summary: Center Robert Hainsey left with a left knee injury and Danny Striggow went into concussion evaluation. Neither returned. Running back Bhayshul Tuten played through a foot and ankle issue that kept him out of practice Wednesday and Thursday, and finished with 88 rushing yards.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence throws for 352 and three scores
stories.summary: Lawrence completed passes to nine different receivers, and the 352 yards were the fourth highest total of his career. Parker Washington caught the opening touchdown and finished with a career-high 152 yards. Cam Little kicked four field goals.

stories.text: 148: Parker Washington's yards by halftime
stories.summary: Washington had 148 of his 152 receiving yards before the break. He caught a 2-yard touchdown to open the scoring. Jacksonville led 16-10 at halftime and scored 17 in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Jaguars visit the Giants on Sunday
stories.summary: Jacksonville plays at the New York Giants on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the center spot if Hainsey sits, and how the new defensive additions from the deadline, Jordan Davis, Davon Godchaux and Jessie Bates III, fit in.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans still winless at home after loss

stories.text: Titans fall to 1-8, still winless at home
stories.summary: Jacksonville beat Tennessee 40-23 at Nissan Stadium. The Titans are 0-5 at home this season and have lost five straight to the Jaguars. A late Tony Pollard touchdown cut the deficit to 30-23 before Jacksonville closed it out.

stories.text: Adams in concussion protocol, Skoronski on IR
stories.summary: Safety Tony Adams left with a concussion. Earlier in the week the Titans put left guard Peter Skoronski and punter Tommy Townsend on injured reserve. Chandler Zavala started at left guard.

stories.text: Cam Ward hits a career-long 50-yarder
stories.summary: Ward connected with Elic Ayomanor on a 50-yard catch and run, the longest completion of his young career. He also threw a 2-yard touchdown to Daniel Bellinger and a 32-yard dump-off to Pollard. Tennessee gained 327 yards of total offense.

stories.text: 0-5: Titans' record at Nissan Stadium
stories.summary: Tennessee has lost all five home games this season. Overall the Titans are 1-8 and last in the AFC South. They have not beaten Jacksonville since the franchise record run began five games ago.

stories.text: Titans travel to Dallas on Sunday
stories.summary: Tennessee plays at the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at AT&T Stadium. The Titans need a road game to end a run of home losses. Watch the guard and safety injury situations.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos rest at 7-2 with Raiders next

stories.text: Broncos use Week 10 bye to sit atop the AFC West at 7-2
stories.summary: Denver is off this week with a five-game winning streak and the AFC West lead. Sean Payton is 4-0 in the last game before a bye and 3-0 right after one. The Athletic's playoff simulator gives the Broncos a 57% shot at the division title.

stories.text: Secondary losses pile up before the bye
stories.summary: Safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones missed the win over Carolina, and cornerback Riley Moss left after 17 snaps. Receiver Jaylen Waddle left with a concussion after 14 snaps. RJ Harvey has not played since Week 7, and Payton says he will return shortly. The bye gives all of them extra time, but no current statuses have been posted.

stories.text: Rookie Jonah Coleman takes over the backfield
stories.summary: Coleman's snap share climbed from 49% to 66% to 77% over the last three games, while J.K. Dobbins fell to 15%. Against Carolina he ran 17 times for 57 yards, caught four passes for 31 and scored from 9 yards out. Since Week 7 he has 152 yards on 37 carries, and he should lead the group after the bye.

stories.text: 29.7%: Denver's third-down rate is the NFL's worst
stories.summary: The Broncos have converted 30 of 101 third downs and still sit at 7-2. In their four-game win streak before Carolina they converted just 18.8%, which DNVR and Opta called the lowest mark by any team during a four-game winning streak this century. Fixing it is the top job for the stretch run.

stories.text: Raiders visit Denver on Sunday, Nov. 22
stories.summary: Denver hosts Las Vegas at Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. The Raiders are 4-6 and will start rookie Fernando Mendoza. After that the Broncos play at Pittsburgh on Friday, Nov. 27, at 3 p.m. ET on Prime Video.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Mahomes throws five TDs in rout of Falcons

stories.text: Chiefs beat Falcons 35-13 and Josh Downs scores in debut
stories.summary: Kansas City won in Atlanta and moved to 7-2. Josh Downs, acquired from Indianapolis earlier in the week, caught three passes for 51 yards and a touchdown in the first half. The defense gave up no touchdowns until Bijan Robinson scored in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Trey Smith in concussion protocol, Wiley fractures ankle
stories.summary: Right guard Trey Smith left in the first quarter and enters the concussion protocol, so his Week 11 status is open. Tight end Jared Wiley fractured his ankle, per Andy Reid. Travis Kelce aggravated his ankle but returned, and Creed Humphrey left late with a minor eye poke. Right tackle Jaylon Moore could return if he practices.

stories.text: Emmett Johnson steps in for Walker and scores twice
stories.summary: Johnson made his first career start with Kenneth Walker out with a groin injury. The rookie ran for 101 yards and added 70 receiving yards with two touchdowns. He has now scored in three straight weeks.

stories.text: 5: touchdown passes for Mahomes, his first such game since 2022
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes went 22 of 35 for 348 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions, a 141.2 rating. It was his seventh career five-touchdown game. Only Drew Brees, Tom Brady and Peyton Manning have more.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Arrowhead on Sunday, Nov. 22
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts Arizona (3-7) at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Chiefs then play the Bills on Thanksgiving. Watch the offensive line, where Smith, Moore and Humphrey all carry questions.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza's first start ends in loss to Seattle

stories.text: Raiders fade in the second half and fall to Seahawks 21-13
stories.summary: Las Vegas led early in Fernando Mendoza's first NFL start but lost at Allegiant Stadium and dropped to 4-6. It was the third one-possession loss of the season. After a Matt Gay field goal, the offense punted on seven straight possessions and gained 24 yards in that stretch.

stories.text: Brock Bowers hurts ankle and sits out second half
stories.summary: Bowers hurt his ankle early while run blocking. He returned briefly, then was ruled out for the second half after two catches for 18 yards. No designation or practice report has been posted yet for the Denver game.

stories.text: Fernando Mendoza starts fast, then gets swarmed
stories.summary: The No. 1 overall pick opened with a 3-for-3 drive and a 10-yard touchdown run. He went 11 of 13 for 90 yards in the first half and led the team in rushing with 21 yards. Seattle's pass rush took over after halftime. Full-game passing totals were not in the recap.

stories.text: 0-for-7: Raiders on third down in the second half
stories.summary: Las Vegas never converted a third down after halftime and scored no points in the half. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had one catch for 11 yards in the first half, then 160 yards and a touchdown after the break. Seattle also finished with six sacks and 12 quarterback hits on Mendoza.

stories.text: Raiders travel to Denver for a divisional test
stories.summary: Las Vegas visits the 7-2 Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday, Nov. 22, on CBS. NFL.com and Yahoo list a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Denver comes off its bye and leads the league in quarterback pressures, which is a tough draw for Mendoza.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers visit Ravens on Monday night

stories.text: Winless Chargers try to find a spark in Baltimore
stories.summary: Los Angeles is 0-8 and the last winless team in the NFL. The Chargers lost 44-22 at home to Houston in Week 9. They play at Baltimore tonight.

stories.text: Ladd McConkey out with back spasms
stories.summary: McConkey was questionable Friday and was ruled out Sunday with back spasms. He will not travel to Baltimore. Rashawn Slater is on injured reserve, which hurts the offensive line. McConkey's next chance to return is Nov. 22 against the Jets.

stories.text: Quentin Johnston leads a thin receiver room
stories.summary: Johnston caught a 58-yard touchdown against Houston, the team's first score since Week 5. With McConkey out, Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith carry the receiving load against Baltimore.

stories.text: 8: sacks Justin Herbert took against Houston, a career high
stories.summary: The Texans sacked Herbert eight times while the Chargers defense managed one. Los Angeles converted 5 of 17 third downs and allowed a season-high 485 yards. Stroud threw for 384 yards and five touchdowns.

stories.text: Monday Night Football at Baltimore, 8:15 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The Chargers play the Ravens tonight at M&T Bank Stadium on ESPN. Baltimore is starting newly acquired Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. Next Sunday, Nov. 22, Los Angeles hosts the Jets at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys score 40 and still lose to 49ers

stories.text: Cowboys' defense collapses in a 46-40 loss to San Francisco
stories.summary: Dallas led 17-16 at the half, then gave up 29 points and 340 yards after the break. Brian Schottenheimer called the second-half defense unacceptable and pointed to missed tackles and long plays. At 4-6, the Cowboys still have a mathematical path to the NFC East title, but the margin for error is gone.

stories.text: Bland, Booker and Ogbonnia all leave the 49ers game hurt
stories.summary: Cornerback DaRon Bland hurt his ankle in the first half and did not return. Right guard Tyler Booker also went down with an ankle injury and T.J. Bass replaced him. Defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia left in the second quarter with a finger injury. No post-game updates have come out yet.

stories.text: George Pickens catches three touchdowns and 145 yards
stories.summary: Pickens turned 18 targets into 11 catches, 145 yards and three scores, a career high for touchdowns. His TDs covered 35, 39 and 5 yards. Dak Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns, tying his career high.

stories.text: 584: yards the 49ers gained against Dallas
stories.summary: San Francisco piled up 584 total yards. Brock Purdy threw for a career-best 389, and Christian McCaffrey added 223 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns, two of them on catches of 74 and 66 yards.

stories.text: Cowboys host Titans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Dallas is home against Tennessee on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET. Watch the tackling drills Schottenheimer promised and whether the Bland and Booker injuries cost the Cowboys starters.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants still lead East after last-minute loss

stories.text: Giants fall 24-21 to Washington on a 57-second drive
stories.summary: J.J. McCarthy hit Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard touchdown to put New York ahead in the fourth quarter. Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs answered with a 32-yard score with 57 seconds left, and McCarthy's last pass was intercepted. It was the Giants' first division loss, and they still lead the NFC East at 5-3-1.

stories.text: Pinnock hurts his back; two concussions cleared
stories.summary: Safety Jason Pinnock left early in the third quarter with a back injury. Kayvon Thibodeaux and Bryan Hudson both cleared concussion checks during the game. Edge rusher Brian Burns has been out since early in the season.

stories.text: Isaiah Likely posts a career-best 127 yards
stories.summary: Likely caught nine passes for a career-high 127 yards, including the 66-yard touchdown that gave the Giants a 21-17 lead. Cam Skattebo also returned from a hamstring absence with 78 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 18 carries.

stories.text: 18.9%: the Giants' pass pressure rate, last in the NFL
stories.summary: New York has 17 sacks this season, among the lowest totals in the league, and the worst pressure rate. The Giants got one sack against Washington, a week after a season-high seven.

stories.text: Giants host Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22
stories.summary: New York is home against Jacksonville on Sunday, Nov. 22, then faces San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland and Detroit. Watch whether the pass rush returns and whether McCarthy bounces back from the final interception.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles use bye to weigh staff changes

stories.text: Eagles reach the bye at 2-7 with staff changes on the table
stories.summary: Philadelphia has lost seven straight after a 19-11 loss to the Giants. Nick Sirianni says he will look at himself first and has not ruled out changes. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is the likely target, with the offense ranked 32nd in yards.

stories.text: Zack Baun's back injury adds to a long Eagles list
stories.summary: Linebacker Zack Baun left the Giants game in the third quarter with a back injury and did not return. DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) were inactive. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots.

stories.text: Saquon Barkley plays through hamstring and back injuries
stories.summary: Barkley has been on a pitch count with hamstring and back problems. In the 27-10 loss to Washington he ran 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown. Reports say he will not be traded.

stories.text: 32nd: where the Eagles' offense ranks in total yards
stories.summary: Philadelphia ranks 32nd in yards and 30th in scoring. The offense has not topped 341 yards in a game this season, and the team has lost seven straight for the first time since 2012.

stories.text: Eagles host Steelers Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Philadelphia is off this week and returns Sunday, Nov. 22 against Pittsburgh. The NFL moved the game from the 4:25 p.m. window to 1 p.m. on CBS. Watch who calls the plays after the bye.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Daniels and Diggs rescue Commanders on bye

stories.text: Commanders rally to beat Giants 24-21 and stay alive
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels threw two interceptions, then led the winning drive. Stefon Diggs caught a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. Washington moved to 3-5-1, holds the tiebreaker over New York, and sat out Sunday's slate.

stories.text: Terry McLaurin out for the season; Lucas Patrick in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Wide receiver Terry McLaurin is out for the year. Center Lucas Patrick missed the Giants game with a concussion, and tight end Colson Yankoff was out with a knee injury. Chig Okonkwo hurt his back in the second quarter and came back after halftime.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels goes 23 of 33 with three touchdowns
stories.summary: Daniels threw for 249 yards and three touchdowns against the Giants, though two interceptions nearly sank the night. He also ran 10 times for 28 yards. Diggs's winning score was his 80th career receiving touchdown.

stories.text: 80: career receiving touchdowns for Stefon Diggs
stories.summary: Diggs's 32-yard catch with 57 seconds left was his 80th career receiving touchdown. Only 30 players in NFL history have reached that mark.

stories.text: Commanders host Bengals on Monday, Nov. 23
stories.summary: Washington had no game Sunday after Thursday's win and hosts Cincinnati on Monday, Nov. 23, then plays at Arizona and at Tennessee. A win could push Washington past Dallas for second in the division.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears hit the bye at 7-2 in a three-way tie

stories.text: Bears reach the bye week 7-2 and tied for the division lead
stories.summary: Chicago beat Tampa Bay 27-24 on Sunday Night Football in Week 9 and has won four straight. The Bears sit at 7-2 alongside Detroit and Minnesota after Minnesota's win in Green Bay. Four division games remain, including Thanksgiving in Detroit and a season finale at Minnesota.

stories.text: Burden's concussion and Williams' hamstring get a week to heal
stories.summary: Receiver Luther Burden III left the Tampa Bay game with a concussion after seven catches for 97 yards and a touchdown, and his status for the Saints is uncertain. Quarterback Caleb Williams uses the bye to rest a sore hamstring. Running back Kyle Monangai, lineman Dayo Odeyingbo and cornerbacks Tyrique Stevenson and Malik Muhammad have all missed time and need to get healthy.

stories.text: Austin Booker keeps climbing with a career-high five sacks
stories.summary: Booker has five sacks and six tackles for loss, both career highs, and coach Ben Johnson says he keeps improving. Linebacker Devin Bush also earned praise for one of his best games as a Bear against Tampa Bay. Odeyingbo, who has three sacks, could line up inside next to Jeffery Simmons or outside opposite Montez Sweat when he returns.

stories.text: 17: giveaways for a 7-2 team that sits at minus 4 in turnovers
stories.summary: Chicago has 17 giveaways (nine interceptions, eight lost fumbles) against 13 takeaways. Ten of those giveaways came in two games, five each against Green Bay and Tampa Bay. Williams threw four interceptions against the Bucs after throwing none in his previous three starts.

stories.text: Saints visit Soldier Field Sunday, then a Thanksgiving trip
stories.summary: Chicago had its bye in Week 10 and hosts New Orleans on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Four days later the Bears play at Detroit on Thanksgiving at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the turnover count and Burden's availability.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions rout Patriots in Munich, lose Hutchinson

stories.text: Lions beat the Patriots 35-10 in Munich to reach 7-2
stories.summary: Detroit ran and passed past New England in Germany. The Lions own the NFC North tiebreaker over Minnesota and Green Bay with a 2-0 division record. The win came with a cost when Aidan Hutchinson went down in the first quarter.

stories.text: Hutchinson's right knee injury is reported as season-ending
stories.summary: Hutchinson hurt his right knee landing from a sack celebration and left the stadium on crutches. The AP, citing an anonymous source, reported a season-ending injury. The Lions have not confirmed a diagnosis. He had an MRI in Germany and will seek second opinions, and coach Dan Campbell said the team would know more back in the States.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs piles up 252 yards from scrimmage
stories.summary: Gibbs ran 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns and caught seven passes for 99 yards. He did it against a Patriots run defense that had allowed 96.7 yards a game, ninth fewest in the league. He had 171 of his yards in the first half.

stories.text: 5: sacks for Detroit, four of them after Hutchinson left
stories.summary: Rookie Derrick Moore had two sacks, and DJ Wonnum and Alim McNeill each added one. Hutchinson had the other, on a New England third down in the first quarter. Moore's two-sack day gives Detroit a first look at life without its top pass rusher.

stories.text: Buccaneers visit Ford Field Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Tampa Bay on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Tampa Bay is 3-6 and quarterback Baker Mayfield is dealing with a lower leg injury. Then the Lions host Chicago on Thanksgiving.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers fall 30-10 to Vikings, eight sacks hurt

stories.text: Vikings bury Packers 30-10 at Lambeau, Green Bay at 6-4
stories.summary: Green Bay fell behind 20-0 and never recovered. The Packers lost three fumbles, each leading to a Vikings field goal, and turned the ball over four times in all. They are 1-3 in the division and sit two games back in the loss column of the three teams at 7-2.

stories.text: Three Packers leave early; Parsons return expected soon
stories.summary: Cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), returner Skyy Moore (ankle) and receiver Bo Melton (thigh) left in the first half. Josh Jacobs needs the extra week of rest to heal. Reports point to Micah Parsons returning around the Rams game.

stories.text: Xavier McKinney grabs his sixth interception of the year
stories.summary: McKinney picked off Kirk Cousins, the Packers' only takeaway of the afternoon. It was his sixth of the season. After the game he said the team will not lose confidence and insisted it is not over.

stories.text: 8: sacks of Jordan Love, most Green Bay has allowed since 2015
stories.summary: Minnesota's eight sacks were its most in a game since 2018. Love finished 17 of 27 for 220 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Levi Drake Rodriguez had two of the sacks.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then at the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve
stories.summary: Green Bay is off this Sunday. The Packers play at the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix. Then comes a Dec. 6 trip to New Orleans.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Cousins returns, Vikings sack Love eight times

stories.text: Cousins wins his Vikings return as Minnesota routs Green Bay
stories.summary: Kirk Cousins, back after the trade with Las Vegas, went 21 of 31 for 207 yards and two touchdowns in a 30-10 win at Lambeau Field. The Vikings snapped a two-game losing streak and have beaten Green Bay in five of six meetings. They are 7-2 and tied for the division lead.

stories.text: Richter's foot and Jones' shoulder lead the Vikings' list
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Bo Richter left in the first quarter with a foot injury. Receiver Jeshaun Jones hurt his shoulder, returned, and likely faces an MRI. Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson were both out.

stories.text: Justin Jefferson posts season highs in catches and targets
stories.summary: Jefferson caught nine passes on 13 targets, both season highs, for 74 yards. Rookies Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew each caught their first career touchdown from Cousins, from 38 and 20 yards. Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones combined for 106 rushing yards on 27 carries.

stories.text: 8: sacks, Minnesota's most in a game since 2018
stories.summary: The Vikings brought Jordan Love down eight times, with Levi Drake Rodriguez getting two. Harrison Smith also intercepted Love in the end zone. Green Bay lost three fumbles, and each one turned into Vikings points.

stories.text: Vikings face the 49ers in Mexico City on Sunday night
stories.summary: Minnesota plays San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City. Watch how Cousins handles a second start and who is healthy at receiver.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Chiefs roll Falcons, 3-7 heading into bye

stories.text: Chiefs run past Falcons 35-13 as losses pile up
stories.summary: Kansas City took a 7-0 lead on an 80-yard opening drive and pulled away after an offsides penalty erased a field goal try just before halftime. Patrick Mahomes then found Josh Downs for a touchdown. Atlanta fell to 3-7, its third straight loss, and sits last in the NFC South.

stories.text: London leaves with concussion evaluation
stories.summary: Receiver Drake London went through concussion evaluation late against Kansas City and did not return. No further update has come from the team. Before the game, Zachariah Branch was ruled out and edge rusher James Pearce Jr. was listed as questionable. Running back Brian Robinson Jr. went on injured reserve after the Madrid loss.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson keeps finding the end zone
stories.summary: Robinson scored his seventh touchdown of 2026 against the Chiefs and recorded his 12th run of 15 yards or more this season. A week earlier in Madrid he ran for 100 yards and piled up 147 yards from scrimmage against Cincinnati.

stories.text: 11: Hellams tackles in his first start
stories.summary: Safety DeMarcco Hellams led Atlanta with 11 tackles in his first start of the season, filling in after the trade of Jessie Bates. No Falcons defender had that many in a first start of a year, outside Week 1, since Troy Andersen had 13 in 2022.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then a trip to Minnesota
stories.summary: Atlanta is off this weekend. The Falcons return Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET at the Vikings, then host the Lions on Dec. 6. The bye gives London time to clear the concussion protocol.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers win on last-second kick, take the lead

stories.text: Fitzgerald's 54-yarder lifts Panthers to first place
stories.summary: Carolina beat New Orleans 20-17 in the Superdome when Ryan Fitzgerald hit a 54-yard field goal as time expired. The Saints had tied it at 17 with 41 seconds left. The Panthers survived 17 penalties and moved to 4-5, first in the NFC South.

stories.text: Phillips returns, secondary gets reinforcements
stories.summary: Edge rusher Jaelan Phillips came back after missing three games and finished with five tackles, three for loss, plus a sack and a fumble recovery. Earlier in the week Xavier Legette, Jonathon Brooks and Mike Jackson opened 21-day practice windows. Tackle Ikem Ekwonu remains on the physically unable to perform list.

stories.text: Hubbard carries the offense in New Orleans
stories.summary: Chuba Hubbard ran 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and added five catches for 80 yards. Several of those catches set up the late go-ahead drive. Bryce Young finished 17 of 30 for 200 yards.

stories.text: 17: penalties, 152 yards, and Carolina still won
stories.summary: The Panthers were flagged 17 times for 152 yards, a repeat of the discipline problems from Week 9. A 30-yard pass interference call on New Orleans helped set up the winning kick. Carolina has to clean that up before it hosts a Ravens team that is also 4-5.

stories.text: Ravens visit Charlotte on Sunday
stories.summary: Carolina hosts Baltimore on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Panthers then play at Tampa Bay on Monday, Nov. 30 at 8:15 p.m. ET in a game with first place at stake.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints fall late to Panthers at home

stories.text: Saints lose 20-17 on a last-play field goal
stories.summary: Charlie Smyth tied the game at 17 with a 55-yard field goal with 41 seconds left, but Carolina's Ryan Fitzgerald won it from 54 yards as time expired. New Orleans dropped to 3-6, 0-2 in the division and 1-4 at home. The Saints visit the Bears next.

stories.text: Werner and Richards hurt in the loss
stories.summary: Linebacker Pete Werner left in the first half with a hamstring injury, and right tackle Asim Richards left in the second half with a knee injury. Center Erik McCoy left the Week 9 win over Cleveland with a biceps injury.

stories.text: Rookie Jordyn Tyson leads the Saints in catches
stories.summary: Tyson, in his second game after missing seven, caught 11 passes for 80 yards against Carolina. Tyler Shough went 25 of 35 for 187 yards with a touchdown, an interception and a lost fumble. Alvin Kamara scored twice.

stories.text: 1-4: the Saints' record at home
stories.summary: New Orleans has won once in five games in the Superdome this season, and that win came in overtime over Cleveland the week before. Chris Olave caught three passes for 30 yards against the Panthers.

stories.text: Saints head to Chicago
stories.summary: New Orleans plays at the Bears on Sunday, Nov. 22. Chicago is 7-2 and just beat Tampa Bay on a walk-off field goal. Watch the Saints' run defense and whether Werner and Richards can play.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs use bye to heal, Mayfield in question

stories.text: Mayfield's foot and ankle clouds the bye week
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield hurt his foot and ankle in the 27-24 loss at Chicago and has worked in and out of a walking boot during the bye. Sources told ESPN the injury is not long-term and injured reserve is not under discussion. Tampa Bay sits a half game out of first place in the NFC South.

stories.text: Winfield gets two weeks to heal his ankle
stories.summary: Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. missed the Chicago game with a right ankle injury. Coach Todd Bowles has given no timeline, but the bye gives Winfield two weeks before Detroit. Ifeatu Melifonwu filled in against the Bears.

stories.text: Bucky Irving gets a workload check
stories.summary: Irving ran 20 times for 97 yards and two touchdowns at Chicago. He has 111 carries over the last five games, and the Bucs plan to manage his load. Kenny Gainwell added 60 yards on three carries.

stories.text: 21: takeaways, the most in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay leads the league with 21 takeaways, including 16 interceptions, and owns a plus-7 turnover margin. The defense forced five more in Chicago, but Mayfield's two interceptions, one a pick-six, kept the Bucs from cashing in.

stories.text: Lions in Detroit after the bye
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Lions are 7-2. The Bucs have lost three straight against NFC North teams and then host Carolina on Monday, Nov. 30.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Rookie Beck gets buried in first start

stories.text: Carson Beck's first start ends in a 34-6 loss to the Rams
stories.summary: Third-string rookie Carson Beck took over because Gardner Minshew is done for the year, and the Rams made it a long day. Los Angeles sacked Beck five times and turned two Arizona turnovers into short fields. The Cardinals have lost four straight to fall to 3-7.

stories.text: Minshew lands on injured reserve with a suspected torn UCL
stories.summary: Gardner Minshew hurt his right elbow on a hard hit in the Week 9 loss to Seattle. He went on injured reserve and Adam Schefter reported he is not expected to play again this season. Receiver Michael Wilson (neck) is also reported done for the year, which leaves the passing game thin.

stories.text: Trey McBride stays the one dependable target
stories.summary: In the Week 9 loss to Seattle, McBride caught 7 of his 8 targets for 54 yards, including a fourth-down grab late in the fourth quarter. With the receiver room depleted, the tight end is the player the offense keeps looking for.

stories.text: 123: total yards the Cardinals managed against the Rams
stories.summary: Arizona's offense never found a rhythm in Beck's debut. He threw two interceptions and went down five times as the Rams won 34-6.

stories.text: Cardinals head to Kansas City on Sunday
stories.summary: Arizona plays at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch whether Beck holds up against a Chiefs pass rush after taking five sacks this week.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams roll Arizona for fourth straight win

stories.text: Rams beat Arizona 34-6 without Nacua and Adams
stories.summary: Los Angeles won its fourth straight and moved to 6-4, tied with Green Bay and Seattle for the last NFC playoff spot. Matthew Stafford spread the ball around while the top two receivers sat. The defense has not allowed an offensive touchdown in back-to-back games.

stories.text: Nacua goes to IR with knee and toe sprains
stories.summary: Puka Nacua hurt his right knee and big toe on the last offensive snap against Washington and is on injured reserve. With the Week 11 bye, Week 15 is the earliest he can return. Davante Adams, out with a hamstring injury, has a return after Week 12 viewed as realistic. Centers Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon both left the Arizona game.

stories.text: Blake Corum runs for 100 yards in Arizona
stories.summary: Corum carried 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and added three catches. It was his second career 100-yard game. Konata Mumpfield also stepped up with three catches for 81 yards, including a 44-yarder on third-and-7.

stories.text: 0: offensive touchdowns allowed, two games running
stories.summary: The Rams sacked Carson Beck five times and gave up no offensive touchdown for a second straight week. Stafford did throw an interception for the fourth game in a row, the one blemish.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
stories.summary: Los Angeles rests in Week 11. It returns Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8 p.m. ET against Green Bay at SoFi Stadium, streamed on Netflix. Expect the extra days to help the banged-up receiver room and offensive line.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers survive 46-40 shootout in Dallas

stories.text: 49ers outlast Cowboys 46-40 to reach 8-1
stories.summary: San Francisco piled up 584 yards and six touchdowns at AT&T Stadium and won its fourth straight over Dallas. It is the franchise's second 8-1 start in 15 years, after the 2019 team that reached the Super Bowl. New receiver Keenan Allen debuted with five catches for 61 yards after three practices.

stories.text: Deebo Samuel returns, rookie Halton is done for the year
stories.summary: Samuel came back from a three-game hamstring absence and scored twice. Rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton broke his left ankle in Week 9 and is out for the season. Cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) left that game, and Mike Evans was out with Achilles tendinitis. Updated statuses were not available.

stories.text: Christian McCaffrey scores three times in Dallas
stories.summary: McCaffrey finished with 223 scrimmage yards: 161 receiving and 62 rushing. He scored on a 16-yard run and on catches of 74 and 66 yards from Brock Purdy.

stories.text: 389: Brock Purdy's career-high passing yards
stories.summary: Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards and did not throw an interception. He averaged almost 14 yards per attempt in the win.

stories.text: 49ers fly to Mexico City to face Minnesota
stories.summary: San Francisco plays the Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NFL Network. The team will spend a week of altitude training in Colorado Springs first. Seattle visits Levi's Stadium the Sunday after.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks rally past Raiders, head to bye

stories.text: Seahawks rally to beat Raiders 21-13 before the bye
stories.summary: Seattle trailed 10-7 at halftime in Las Vegas and won 21-13 behind a second-half surge. The defense spoiled the first start of Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza. The Seahawks go into the bye at 6-4.

stories.text: Darnold's quad keeps Drew Lock in the lineup
stories.summary: Sam Darnold missed his second straight game with a quad injury, so Drew Lock made his third start. Lock was limited in practice all week with elbow and oblique issues. Reports named Abe Lucas and Jarren Reed among players hurt Sunday, with no details on severity yet. The bye gives the team time to heal.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba breaks the game open with a 71-yard score
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba caught a 71-yard touchdown in the third quarter to push Seattle ahead. Cooper Kupp also scored on a 34-yard pass from Lock, who made a play with his legs on that drive.

stories.text: 6: second-half sacks of Fernando Mendoza, a season high
stories.summary: Seattle's pass rush took over after halftime and sacked the No. 1 overall pick six times. Mendoza was making his first start against the league's top-ranked defense.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then a trip to San Francisco
stories.summary: Seattle is off in Week 11. It plays at the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. San Francisco leads the division at 8-1, so the NFC West race runs through this game.
